Context: Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (React/Chakra), Confluence space key SFCC. I am pre-build planning:
- SFCC-236 "Product Card Shared Component" — ONE shared product card component with display variations driven by a style prop.
- SFCC-83 / SFCC-84 "Recently Viewed" UI component and full-history page.

Your job is a THOROUGH SEARCH SWEEP. I need to know what documentation exists AND, just as importantly, what does NOT exist.

Run mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search with spaces_filter="SFCC" for each of these (separate calls, limit 15 each). Use plain-text queries unless noted:
- "product card"
- "product tile"
- "shared component"
- "component library"
- "design system"
- "atomic design"
- "atoms molecules organisms"
- "Storybook"
- "browsing history"
- "See Full History"
- "wishlist page"
- "homepage product"
- text ~ "Technical Solution Design"
- text ~ "TSD"

Also call mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_space_page_tree with space_key="SFCC" and limit=250, and scan the returned titles for anything that looks like: a TSD, a component/design-system page, a PLP page spec, a Homepage page spec, a Wishlist page spec, or a Recently Viewed page. Report the promising titles + IDs you spot in the tree even if the keyword searches missed them.

Then OPEN and read the most promising 5-8 pages you find and report on each: exact page title, page ID, version number, any last-updated date in the body, and a tight summary of ONLY what is relevant to (i) how a shared/reusable component should be structured and built, (ii) what a product tile/card must contain on PLP, Homepage, or Wishlist, (iii) recently viewed / browsing history.

Note: I have ALREADY covered these pages myself — do not re-read or report on them, just note if something links to them:
- 392888324 (TSD parent) and its 15 children
- 303661057 (04.1.9 Search and Recommendations)
- 302612483 (04.1.12 Price, Currency and Promotions)
- 302776322 (04.1.8 Product, Catalogue and PDP)
- 400195591 (04.7 Component Inventory)
- 408944644 (04.72 Component Design & User Story Tracker)
- 258801666 (04.2 Design Tracker)
- 299433985 (04.6 Consent Management)

CRITICAL DELIVERABLE: an explicit list of which of these topics have NO documentation at all in the space:
(a) a TSD covering product card / shared components
(b) a TSD or design doc covering recently viewed / browsing history storage
(c) a design-system / atomic-structure / component-build-standards page
(d) a page specifying Homepage product tile contents
(e) a page specifying Wishlist page tile contents
(f) a page specifying a "See Full History" / full browsing history page

"No page exists for X" is a first-class finding I need, not a failure. Be precise about the difference between "I searched and found nothing" and "I found something tangential". Do not pad with irrelevant pages.

Do NOT create, update, or comment on any Confluence page. Read-only. Do not write any files. Return findings directly as your final message.

content.text:
Sweep complete. Full space tree retrieved and verified complete (284 pages, `has_more: false`), so the "no page exists" findings below are exhaustive against titles, plus 14 keyword/CQL searches against body text.

## Pages I opened and read (not on your covered list)

**1. `04.71 Writing User Stories for Components` — ID 400195600, v2** (child of 04.7)
The closest thing in the space to a component-build standard, but it's a *story-writing* standard, not a build standard. Two levels: Level 1 = component epics (build story per component: "what the component does, its variants and configurations, accessibility requirements, and any error or empty states"), Level 2 = page epics (how components compose into a journey, shopper perspective, "should not repeat the component build detail from Level 1"). Splits components into **PWA Kit only** (one story) vs **Contentful + PWA Kit** (two stories — content model story + render story). Nothing about file structure, props API, variant/style-prop patterns, or Storybook. Directly relevant to SFCC-236: a shared product card driven by a style prop is a Level 1 component epic, and its PLP/Homepage/Wishlist usages are Level 2 page epics.

**2. `Component Override Strategy` — ID 261881857, v4** (under 05.2 → Development Standards)
The only page describing how to physically build a component. Covers the slim-overrides model, the copy-first override procedure (copy base → convert to TS → `npx tsc --noEmit` → temporary `console.log` to confirm the override renders → only then make functional changes), keep upstream kebab-case for overrides. **Stale on the key point for SFCC-236:** it says new Zimmermann components go under `overrides/app/components/custom/` — the repo actually uses `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/`. Nothing here about shared/variant-driven components at all.

**3. `Development Standards` — ID 261750785, v2** (parent of the above)
Naming table, TS-only rule, Storybook categorisation table (`Foundation/ Elements/ Commerce/ Layout/ Forms/ Pages/`), three testing layers, protection tiers. Two more staleness traps for a build plan: it tells you to import icons from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons` (AGENTS.md now forbids this — use `overrides/app/components/icons`), and its worked token example uses bare Chakra keys (`color="brand.primary"` / `fontSize="md"`), which `overrideStyling.md` now forbids in favour of `var(--zimm-*)` and is mechanically failed by `recipeGuards.test.ts`.

**4. `Design Decision Tracker` — ID 449282049, v1 — EMPTY.** Third child of 04.7 Component Inventory. Version 1, no body content at all. Title suggests it was meant to hold exactly the kind of per-component decision you'd want for SFCC-236; it holds nothing.

**5. `04.1.1 Homepage and Content` — ID 303071234, v14.** 40 requirements HPC-001→040. Sole source of truth = Zimmermann Functional Requirements Excel, downloaded 3 Jul 2026. **Contains zero product-tile/card requirements.** Entirely Contentful authoring, Didomi consent gating, header nav, footer. The closest is HPC-009: "should support editorial modules including campaign imagery, collection features and product spotlights" (Confirmed) — no tile contents behind it.

**6. `04.1.11 Customers, Account, CRM Sync` — ID 302022672, v16.** 200+ CRM-prefixed requirements, extracted 3 Jul 2026. Wishlist is 31 rows across four sub-areas (PLP ×7, PDP ×10, Global ×2, My Account ×12). The load-bearing one for you:

> **CRM-132** (Confirmed) — "The system will display the customer's saved wishlist items on the My Account Wishlist page showing **product image, product name, price, sale price or What's Now price where applicable, size and colour** for each item"

Plus, relevant to a shared card's variant surface: **CRM-113** star icon on every PLP tile; **CRM-115** size-selection popover *on the product tile* showing in-stock sizes only; **CRM-134** greyed-out unavailable state for out-of-region items (kept, not removed); **CRM-131** regional availability marking; **CRM-135** notification banner on wishlist actions.

**7. `04.1.18 Storefront Page Templates` — ID 303333385, v3.** Six one-line rows. Confirms wishlist is a deliverable My Account page template and PLP/search/no-results/PDP are Catalogue Browse templates. **No "recently viewed" or "browsing history" page template listed anywhere** — so a full-history page is not in the template scope list.

**8. `1.5 Web Design (UX)` — ID 268075023, v2.** The design gate. DDP owns design production; "a page or component is **not buildable scope until its design is signed off**." Sign-off tracker (owner "Jasijn Tsang", **last-updated field is blank**) shows Homepage READY, PLP READY, PDP In Review, **Wishlist = DRAFT / "Not ready for build"**. Note this tracker contradicts the 04.7 component-level tracker you've already read — you flagged that two-tracker conflict before; this is the stale page-level one.

**9. `5.9.3 — Component Mapping` — ID 464945168, v7** (last updated in-body 2026-09-02). The **only** page in the entire space that uses atoms/molecules/organisms vocabulary — and it's scoped to Contentful, not the commerce components. Three things matter for SFCC-236:
- It states explicitly that the SFCC-side components under `overrides/app/components/` "weren't built to stand alone, and we can't reuse them for pure-Contentful pages," so Contentful gets its own parallel set under `overrides/app/components/contentful/components/`. A single shared product card crosses that stated boundary.
- **"Sharing tokens, not components"** is the recorded position: reuse the design system (`var(--zimm-*)`, `textStyle`, Chakra props) not the component code.
- It flags a **"Shoppable product caption / product-grid carousel"** as "the single most consistent pattern with zero Jira coverage — 97 of 299 pages." That is a product-card-shaped need with no story behind it; worth deciding whether SFCC-236 is meant to serve it.
- Precedent worth citing in your plan: `ZimmSubscribeSection` (`ui-kits/organisms/`) is named as the one component already deliberately extracted to be placeable on any page — the existing model for "shared, reusable, no SFCC-hook dependency."

## CRITICAL DELIVERABLE — what does NOT exist

Verified against the complete 284-page title list plus body-text search. "Searched and found nothing" vs "found something tangential" is distinguished per item.

**(a) A TSD covering product card / shared components — DOES NOT EXIST.**
Searched and found nothing. The TSD set is complete and enumerable: your 15 covered children of 392888324, plus three others sitting outside that parent (`TSD-SFCC-708 PDP Related Colours` ID 458948614, parented to 05.1 not the TSD hub; `SFCC-49 Country List TSD` ID 453443668, a grandchild under 256835585; `TSD: AI-Assisted Defect Triage Agent` ID 277708843, under 05.5). None is about product cards, tiles, or shared component architecture. The nearest-neighbour TSDs are `TSD-SFCC-225 — Product Badges` and `TSD-SFCC-708 — PDP Related Colours` — both single-feature PDP/tile decorations, neither addresses the card container or a variant API.

**(b) A TSD or design doc covering recently viewed / browsing history storage — DOES NOT EXIST.**
Searched and found nothing. No page title contains "recently" or "browsing". A body search for `localStorage` / `sessionStorage` / "session storage" returns four hits, none of them about recently viewed (INSIDE Tag PDF, CX Data Dictionary, Consent Management, Customer Data Migration). The **only** storage statement anywhere in the space is a single FR clause on 04.1.9 (which you've covered): browsing history "to be stored in the browser session and persisted cross-session on login." There is no design for how, no cap, no dedupe rule, no cross-region behaviour, no anonymous→authenticated merge, and no decision on the open consent question raised in 04.6.
